paper.title_en: Energy accreted onto a compact star
paper.abstract_en: We compute the energy gained by accretion onto a compact star due to matter falling from the inner edge of a thin accretion disk. We employ a controlled slow-rotation expansion based on the Hartle-Thorne metric and find that in neutron stars in general only leading order rotational corrections to the metric, describing frame dragging, are sizable. However, for accretion onto a magnetized neutron star, where the disk roughly extends to the co-rotation radius, even frame dragging effects are minor. Based on general conservation laws we then derive simple, equation-of-state-independent expressions for the spin-up and heating energy, consistently including the relevant rotational, relativistic and nuclear effects, and find that in observed accreting millisecond sources the results can strongly deviate from presently employed estimates.
